subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron quarantine overflow recovery silently delete older persisted archive records after five retained files, or must cleanup remain recoverable and operator-visible?
rationale: The branch changes the recovery-data retention contract rather than fixing a purely mechanical bug; source and tests can prove pruning occurs but cannot determine whether permanent deletion is an acceptable product policy.

options.title: Use recoverable cleanup
options.body: Keep the bounded read and archive rotation, but make archive cleanup doctor-owned or otherwise operator-visible so historical quarantined jobs are not silently discarded.

options.title: Accept five retained archives
options.body: Approve the fixed five-file retention policy and document that repeated overflow recovery permanently deletes the oldest quarantine records.

options.title: Pause archive rotation
options.body: Land only a narrower bounded-read/write behavior after removing the archive-retention design until cron recovery ownership is decided.

recommendation.title: Use recoverable cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded read and archive rotation, but make archive cleanup doctor-owned or otherwise operator-visible so historical quarantined jobs are not silently discarded.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context does not establish a concrete current-main code owner, while the decision is about cron persistence and recovery product policy.
